![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/2206a1bc02acb9ddccc5991a4c8d36c9e5d3255e72239e8f7e81908e10faab48.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=18y$ for $x\ge 0$ and $z\ge 0,$ shown above. 
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}xy\,\text{d}V
$$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $3$ centered at $(0,3,0).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=18y$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =18y \\ {\rho }^{2} & =18\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho -18\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =18\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14158590/assets/578c7f81a0dae8339772dec9a9407fb380866e5dde5fdd18fee04feb6afe5749.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 18\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=xy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}xy\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{18\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$
